name: Ampicillin
indication: Early-Onset & Late-Onset Neonatal Sepsis, Meningitis, L. monocytogenes
recipeRule: Sepsis: 50 mg/kg/dose IV. Meningitis: 100 mg/kg/dose IV. Frequency: Q12H (<7d GA<34w), Q8H (7-28d), Q6H (Meningitis).

name: Gentamicin
indication: Gram-negative Sepsis, E. coli, Pseudomonas, Synergy for GBS
recipeRule: Extended interval dosing: 4-5 mg/kg Q36-48H (<30w GA), Q24-36H (30-34w GA), Q24H (≥35w GA). Trough level <1.0 mcg/mL.

name: Cefotaxime
indication: Neonatal Meningitis, Gram-Negative Sepsis, Suspected Sepsis with Renal Impairment
recipeRule: Meningitis: 50 mg/kg Q12H (<7d), Q8H (7-28d). Sepsis: 50 mg/kg Q12H (<7d), Q8H (>7d).

name: Vancomycin
indication: MRSA, Late-Onset Sepsis, Coagulase-Negative Staph (CONS), Line Infections
recipeRule: 10-15 mg/kg IV over 60 min. Q24H (<29w GA), Q12-18H (29-34w), Q8-12H (≥35w). Target trough 10-15 mcg/mL (15-20 for severe/meningitis).
adverseEffects: Red Man Syndrome (if infused fast), Nephrotoxicity, Ototoxicity
antidote: Antihistamines for Red Man Syndrome, slow infusion

name: Caffeine Citrate
indication: Apnea of Prematurity (AOP), Extubation Facilitation (<32 Weeks)
recipeRule: Loading dose: 20 mg/kg IV/PO once over 30 min. Maintenance: 5-10 mg/kg PO/IV Q24H starting 24h after loading.
adverseEffects: Tachycardia (>180 bpm), restlessness, feeding intolerance, hyperglycemia

name: Beractant / Poractant Alfa (Surfactant)
indication: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) Prevention & Rescue
doseRange: Curosurf: 2.5 mL/kg (200 mg/kg), Survanta: 4 mL/kg (100 mg/kg)
recipeRule: Poractant alfa (Curosurf): 2.5 mL/kg (200 mg/kg) initial ET instillation. Repeat 1.25 mL/kg (100 mg/kg) Q12H x2 doses PRN. LISA / INSURE technique.
adverseEffects: Transient bradycardia, oxygen desaturation, ET tube blockage
antidote: Suction ET tube, increase FiO2 temporarily

name: Epinephrine (Adrenaline)
indication: Neonatal Resuscitation (HR <60 bpm after CPR), Refractory Shock
recipeRule: IV/IO: 0.02 mg/kg (0.2 mL/kg of 1:10,000 solution) rapid push followed by 1 mL NS flush. ET route (if no IV): 0.05-0.1 mg/kg (0.5-1 mL/kg). Infusion: 0.05-1 mcg/kg/min.
adverseEffects: Arrhythmias, severe hypertension, tissue necrosis on extravasation

name: Dopamine
indication: Neonatal Hypotension, Septic Shock, Cardiogenic Shock
standardConcentration: 40 mg/mL vial (Dilute in D5W or NS)
recipeRule: Continuous IV Infusion: Start 5 mcg/kg/min. Titrate up to 20 mcg/kg/min. Recipe: 6 x Weight(kg) = mg Dopamine per 100 mL IV fluid (1 mL/hr = 1 mcg/kg/min).
adverseEffects: Tachycardia, ectopic beats, vasoconstriction, peripheral gangrene

name: Dobutamine
indication: Myocardial Dysfunction, Low Cardiac Output, Post-Resuscitation Myocardial Stunning
recipeRule: Continuous IV Infusion: Start 5 mcg/kg/min. Range 2.5-20 mcg/kg/min. Recipe: 6 x Weight(kg) = mg Dobutamine per 100 mL IV fluid.
adverseEffects: Tachycardia, mild hypotension (due to beta-2 vasodilation), arrhythmias

name: Phenobarbital
indication: First-line Treatment for Neonatal Seizures, Hypoxic Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE)
recipeRule: Loading: 20 mg/kg IV slow push over 20 min. If seizures persist, give additional 5-10 mg/kg (Max total loading 40 mg/kg). Maintenance: 3-5 mg/kg/day PO/IV in 1-2 divided doses.

name: Morphine Sulfate
indication: Analgesia in Mechanical Ventilation, Post-operative Pain, Severe Procedural Pain
recipeRule: Intermittent IV: 0.05-0.1 mg/kg Q4-6H. Continuous IV Infusion: 10-20 mcg/kg/hr. Reduce dose in renal impairment or non-ventilated infants.
adverseEffects: Respiratory depression, hypotension, urinary retention, bowel ileus

name: Furosemide (Lasix)
indication: Fluid Overload, Pulmonary Edema, Heart Failure, BPD Fluid Management
recipeRule: IV/IM: 1 mg/kg Q12-24H. Oral: 1-2 mg/kg Q12-24H. Monitor serum potassium, sodium, and calcium closely.
adverseEffects: Hypokalemia, hyponatremia, ototoxicity (especially with aminoglycosides), nephrocalcinosis
